meta.description: Resolves GWAS associations to candidate causal variants and credible sets via SuSiE, susie_rss, FINEMAP, CAVIAR, DAP-G, PAINTOR, PolyFun, SuSiEx, MultiSuSiE, and FOCUS. Use when narrowing a GWAS lead SNP to a 95 percent credible set, choosing between in-sample and reference LD, calibrating non-sparse loci, integrating functional priors via PolyFun, fine-mapping across ancestries, diagnosing LD mismatch, handling HLA, or feeding credible sets into coloc.susie.

scientific_integrity.detail: All 12 cited papers (Wang 2020 JRSSB 82:1273, Zou 2022 PLoS Genet, Cui 2024 Nat Genet 56:162, Benner 2016 Bioinformatics 32:1493, Weissbrod 2020 Nat Genet 52:1355, Yuan 2024 Nat Genet 56:1841, etc.) are real and correctly attributed; no fabricated statistics, p-values, or sample sizes anywhere in the Skill.

practice_boundaries.detail: Population-genetics / statistical-genomics research workflow only; no individual diagnostic, prescriptive, or treatment claims in scope anywhere in SKILL.md or usage-guide.md.

methodological_ground.detail: The Skill actively guards against the methodological fallacy this audit's adversarial input (Input 7) tried to induce: a dedicated 'Credible-set misinterpretation' section rejects reporting a single top-PIP SNP as causal, and the case-control Neff correction (verified empirically against 4/(1/Ncase+1/Ncontrol)=19800.0) is stated correctly.

code_usability.detail: 6 of 7 executed/inspected code patterns (susie_rss summary-stat, susie individual-level, LD-mismatch diagnostic, L-scaling for non-sparse loci, Neff correction, FINEMAP CLI syntax) ran or checked out cleanly against real planted-truth data or public documentation. One pattern (coloc.susie, Input 4) crashes with a cryptic data.table error when followed exactly as documented in SKILL.md, due to an undocumented precondition (z/R must carry SNP names) -- a real, fixable, one-line gap in a single code block among ~15 documented patterns, not a systemic failure. Recorded as a P1 recommendation rather than a veto.

functional_suitability.note: Covers essentially every fine-mapping method in current use (SuSiE family, FINEMAP, CAVIAR, DAP-G, PAINTOR, PolyFun, SuSiEx, MultiSuSiE, FOCUS) with a correct decision tree by scenario; one verified correctness gap in the coloc.susie example (Input 4).

reliability.note: Excellent explicit handling for LD mismatch, non-convergence, and PSD violations (Category-3 override applied: hard stops are correct design). The coloc.susie SNP-naming precondition is neither validated, warned about, nor listed in the 'Common Errors' table, and the resulting failure is maximally cryptic (unrelated data.table internals).

performance_context.note: SKILL.md is 436 lines with all technical depth (algorithmic taxonomy, thresholds, failure modes, reviewer pushback) inline rather than in a references/ folder that would load conditionally; no references/ directory exists at all. Workflow itself (diagnose -> choose -> fit -> extract -> report) is linear with no redundant steps.

agent_usability.note: Consistent terminology (PIP, credible set, purity, lambda, Neff) throughout; explicit output/reporting expectations (Required Reporting Schema table); one of the strongest 'Per-Tool Failure Modes' + 'Common Errors' catalogs seen in this audit series, though it omits the coloc.susie naming precondition found by execution.

human_usability.note: Natural-language Quick Start prompts in usage-guide.md map precisely onto how a researcher actually asks for this work. Category-3 forgiveness override applied (strict input validation is correct here); documented errors are clear, the one undocumented one (coloc naming) is not.

security.note: No credentials or sensitive data anywhere; only public reference panels (1000G, UKB baseline-LF) cited. Explicit PSD/eigenvalue and convergence checks exist for the summary-statistic path; no equivalent pre-flight check exists for the coloc.susie naming precondition.

maintainability.note: Clean separation across SKILL.md (method/taxonomy), usage-guide.md (workflow/prompts), and examples/ (4 runnable scripts). Every documented code path was independently testable and, in 6/7 cases, verified correct against planted-truth synthetic data.

agent_specific.note: Precise, well-targeted trigger description; excellent composability (12 related Skills cross-referenced with concrete interface descriptions); explicit, strong escape hatches (dedicated 'HLA and Long-Range LD: When to Stop' section). Progressive disclosure is the one weak sub-criterion: no references/ folder exists, so all reference-style tables load with the Skill every time.

inputs.note: L=10 saturated all 10 slots and missed 2/12 planted signals; L=30 auto-pruned to exactly 12 credible sets and recovered all 12 planted causals -- a textbook confirmation of the Skill's 'L is cheap to increase' guidance.

inputs.label: Case-control Neff vs Ntotal + "just tell me THE causal SNP" framing
inputs.note: Neff formula (4/(1/Ncase+1/Ncontrol)) verified exact at 19,800.0 vs Ntotal 500,000 (25.3x). Residual-variance calibration differed materially (0.9957 vs 0.9007, ~10.5%) between the two N choices, confirming the Skill's warning empirically. This locus's signal was strong enough that top-line PIP did not flip -- a property of the chosen synthetic locus, not a Skill defect; the mandated non-single-SNP framing from 'Credible-set misinterpretation' still applies regardless of PIP sharpness.

assertions.text: Neff formula matches 4/(1/Ncase+1/Ncontrol)
Residual-variance/calibration estimate differs materially between Ntotal and Neff fits

key_strengths: The mandatory estimate_s_rss / kriging_rss LD-mismatch diagnostic works exactly as documented: on a genuinely mismatched reference panel, lambda jumped from 0.0000 (matched) to 0.7517 (mismatched) and correctly produced the predicted symptom (9 spurious singleton credible sets vs. the true 1).

L-scaling guidance for high-signal / HLA-like loci verified empirically end-to-end: with 12 planted causal variants, L=10 saturated and missed 2 signals, L=30 recovered all 12 and auto-pruned to exactly 12.

Extensive, well-sourced failure-mode catalog (LD mismatch, non-sparse architecture, L too small, prior_weights vs prior_variance, Neff vs Ntotal, allele harmonization, credible-set misinterpretation) citing real primary literature with correct volume/page numbers.
Case-control Neff correction is correctly specified and shown to materially change the model's residual-variance calibration when tested against a planted-truth locus.
Strong composability: 12 related Skills cross-referenced with concrete, correct interface descriptions (credible sets feed coloc.susie; fine-mapped variants feed MR as cis-instruments).

recommendations.title: coloc.susie example crashes on SKILL.md's own documented code (missing SNP-name precondition)
recommendations.problem: Running the 'Coloc.susie Integration' section's code exactly as written (bare, unnamed z1/z2 vectors) crashes with a cryptic, unrelated data.table error ('Check that is.data.table(DT) == TRUE...') instead of succeeding or failing with a clear message.
recommendations.root_cause: coloc.bf_bf matches SNPs between the two susie fits' lbf_variable matrices via intersect(colnames(bf1), colnames(bf2)); SKILL.md's example never sets names(z1)/names(z2) or LD dimnames, so the intersect is empty, coloc.bf_bf silently returns a summary-less data.table, and coloc.susie's ret$summary[, :=(...)] then fails on NULL.
recommendations.fix: Add one line before the susie_rss calls in the Coloc.susie Integration code block: `names(z1) <- names(z2) <- colnames(ld_matrix) <- rownames(ld_matrix) <- snp_ids`, and state explicitly that coloc.susie requires named SNP IDs on z and R or it fails with an unrelated data.table error.

recommendations.title: No platform caveat for FINEMAP / SuSiEx / PAINTOR / DAP-G (all POSIX-only CLI tools)
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md documents FINEMAP, SuSiEx, PAINTOR, and DAP-G CLI invocations with no mention that these are Linux/macOS-only binaries with no Windows build; an agent running on Windows discovers this only after attempting execution.
recommendations.root_cause: The prerequisites section (usage-guide.md) lists `git clone` / `make` build instructions for each CLI tool without a platform-compatibility note.
recommendations.fix: Add a one-line platform caveat at first mention of each CLI tool: 'Linux/macOS binary only; on Windows use WSL, or fall back to susie_rss for the equivalent inference.'

recommendations.title: SKILL.md carries all technical depth inline rather than in a references/ folder
recommendations.problem: At 436 lines, SKILL.md loads its full Algorithmic Taxonomy, Quantitative Thresholds, and Anticipated Reviewer Pushback tables every time the Skill triggers, rather than deferring this depth to a conditionally-loaded reference file.
recommendations.root_cause: No references/ directory exists for this Skill; all reference-style content lives directly in SKILL.md.
recommendations.fix: Move the Algorithmic Taxonomy, Quantitative Thresholds, and Anticipated Reviewer Pushback tables into references/fine_mapping_reference.md, leaving SKILL.md as a leaner entry point with a pointer to it.

recommendations.title: Individual-level and CLI code paths lack an explicit genotype-QC checklist
recommendations.problem: The summary-statistics path has explicit PSD/eigenvalue and convergence checks; the individual-level susie(X,y) path and the CLI examples have no equivalent guidance on genotype-level quality control (call rate, HWE, MAF floor) before fitting.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill's data-quality guidance is concentrated on the LD-diagnostic block for the summary-statistics path and was not mirrored for the individual-level or CLI paths.
recommendations.fix: Add a brief genotype-QC checklist alongside the susie(X, y) pattern and the FINEMAP/SuSiEx prerequisites.
